analysis:
Two changes were examined. First, NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes was raised from 8<<20 to 40<<20 (head line 369). Second, NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding.encodedHeaderQuote (head lines 224-228) now uses that constant instead of the hard-coded 8 MiB limit. An oversize body now throws the new Failure.bodyTooLarge (head lines 17-18, 226), where it previously threw invalidInput. The template bound (<=1 MiB) and the >0 checks are unchanged.

Security effect: the worst-case ingress reservation rises from about 272 MiB to about 1.3 GiB (body*32 + template*4 + 16 MiB). It is still reserved through the shared VisionMemoryGate ledger (head line 96) before any JSON, base64 or header expansion. A failed reservation still refuses the request with Failure.capacity, so a large adversarial consumer body (ADV-002) is admission-controlled rather than unbounded (TB-007 availability, T-016/T-029 class).

Unchanged controls:
- The 16-image cap.
- The data-URI prefix allowlist, which excludes remote URLs.
- The single-video rule.
- Per-image and per-video plan charges, which use overflow-checked sum/product.
- Release of reservations in settle, skipped under a retained fault.
- Cache scoping, where cacheScope is passed only when prefixBankBytes > 0 (T-041 is unchanged).

The comment states that both transports already cap at 32 MiB (localInferenceMaxUploadBytes and CoordinatorClient.maxInboundMessageBytes). That makes the 40 MiB bound an upper ceiling above the transport limit. Neither constant was in the supplied evidence, so this is unverified.

Integration questions (non-blocking):
- Does the gate's budget make a 1.3 GiB ingress reservation coexist safely with KV reservations? A large body could block other media requests until release, but that is a bounded refusal path.
- How do callers map Failure.bodyTooLarge? Check whether it is surfaced as a non-retryable error and whether exhaustive switches elsewhere still compile and behave fail-closed.

No plaintext exposure, authorization or attestation surface changed. No regression identified.
